# NZ historic bills archive now online

**Originally published:** 23 Poutūterangi 2016

**Last updated:** 23 Poutūterangi 2016

Enlarge image

Historical Bills at New Zealand Parliament Library.

Source: Office of the Clerk

A new archive of New Zealand bills is now available for legal researchers, historians and anyone interested in past legislation.  All bills from 1949 to 2008 are available in the **NZ Historical Bills collection** on the New Zealand Legal Information Institute (NZLII) website.

## Getting NZ’s legislative documents online

The archive is stage one of a digitisation project to get all New Zealand bills online. Bills dating back to 1854 will be added in future stages. Both bills that eventually became Acts and those that were not passed are included in this important collection.   Work on providing as-made Statutory Regulations 1936–2007 is also nearly complete.

## The collection

There’s a wealth of information that captures important moments and decisions in our recent history. There are also laws that are reflections of their time and have since changed.  Some notable bills in the archive include the:

* Capital Punishment Bill 1950 (21-1) which re-introduced the death penalty for about 10 years
* Homosexual Law Reform Bill 1985 (86-1)
* Manapouri -Te Anau Development Bill 1963 (53-1)
* Auckland Harbour Bridge Bill 1950 (120-1)

## Protecting NZ’s historical legislative documents

The collection has been put together from scanned volumes provided by the Parliamentary Counsel Office and the Office of the Clerk.  Most of the volumes were taken apart to enable scanning, but some of the earliest (not yet available online) were too rare to treat in this way. Instead they were scanned using a non-destructive scanner that produces high-quality images from books only partly opened (to avoid damage).

## Other legislation websites

The Historical Bills collection sits alongside others that you might find useful:

* New Zealand Acts 1841–2007 As Enacted
* Bills (proposed laws), Sept 2002 onwards (with links to related parliamentary material)
